name: Thai Village
notes: Router said no-platform on thaivillagepb.com. That site links out to a Smile POS ordering storefront (thaivillageca.smiledining.com), but that platform is a Knockout.js SPA that ships no server-rendered menu data and no discoverable JSON/API endpoint in a reasonable search (guessed /api/menu/<storeId> paths 500'd) -- genuinely needs a browser, naming Smile POS/smiledining.com as a new platform for a Playwright-equipped pass. WebSearch surfaced this restaurant's DoorDash storefront; fetched plain with the Sec-Fetch-*/Upgrade-Insecure-Requests headers, it returned 200 with a full schema.org Menu graph in ld+json (hasMenuSection again nested as [[...]], flattened per the known quirk). Address confirmed via the same ld+json (4618 Mission Boulevard, San Diego) matching the work-list branch exactly. 91 raw items; dropped the 12-item 'Most Ordered' carousel entirely since every item in it (Pad See Ew, Pad Thai, House Curry Panang, Cream Cheese Wonton, Spicy Noodle, Fresh Roll, Yellow Curry, Thai Fried Rice, Green Curry, Avocado Curry, Crispy Spring Roll, Thai Iced Tea) is a verified duplicate of an item already captured in its real category, leaving 79 unique dishes across Appetizers, Soups, Salads, Fruit Curry, Specialties, Entree, Curry, Noodles, Fried Rice, Vegetarian, Side Orders and Drinks -- full core-section coverage for a Thai restaurant (curries, noodles, fried rice, soups all present). No markup pattern found: most entrees sit at a flat $17.95 with curries at $18.95 and apps at $12.95-$15.95, which reads as the restaurant's own uniform category pricing rather than a scattered delivery surcharge. Held at medium rather than high because this is a marketplace listing rather than the restaurant's own site or ordering platform, and no independent cross-check was attempted given time budget.
